## Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic) (`breast_cancer`)

- Source: UCI ML Repository id 17 via scikit-learn load_breast_cancer (bundled CSV) (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/17/breast+cancer+wisconsin+diagnostic)
- SHA-256: `ff5fc1f247213db5fd49539610bcd5a98033bbd0307524fde3127251752aa073`
- Licence: CC BY 4.0
- Provenance: Real clinical: digitised fine-needle-aspirate images, University of Wisconsin Hospitals (1995)
- Target: `diagnosis` in ['malignant'] = malignant
- Dropped columns: none
- Leakage notes: 30 image features of one FNA per patient; no identifiers in the scikit-learn copy.

## Heart Disease (Cleveland) (`heart`)

- Source: UCI ML Repository id 45, processed.cleveland.data (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/heart-disease/processed.cleveland.data)
- SHA-256: `a74b7efa387bc9d108d7d0115d831fe9b414b29ae7124f331b622b4efa0427c8`
- Licence: CC BY 4.0
- Provenance: Real clinical: Cleveland Clinic Foundation angiography cohort (Detrano et al. 1989)
- Target: `num` in ['1', '2', '3', '4'] = heart disease present (num > 0)
- Dropped columns: none
- Leakage notes: Categorical codes (cp, restecg, slope, thal) kept as numeric codes as in v1; 'ca' and 'thal' have a few '?' values imputed in-fold.

## Pima Indians Diabetes (NIDDK; OpenML 37 'diabetes') (`pima`)

- Source: OpenML data_id 37 'diabetes' v1 (from the UCI ML Repository copy donated 1990 by V. Sigillito, JHU APL; original owner NIDDK) (https://openml.org/data/v1/download/37/diabetes.arff)
- SHA-256: `4eddd5b2b64679e8888348e306520a393d6a28e1ddc9643cfb76fc5d912d6d40`
- Licence: Public (OpenML dataset metadata, data_id 37, checked 2026-10-08); no further terms stated; cite Smith et al. 1988 (Proc. SCAMC, pp. 261-265)
- Provenance: Real clinical data: NIDDK study of the Pima Indian population near Phoenix, AZ; 768 women aged >= 21 (Smith et al. 1988). Research examination measurements (OGTT glucose and insulin, BP, skinfold, BMI). Not synthetic. Local MD5 3cbaa3e54586aa88cf6aacb4033e4470 equals OpenML's md5_checksum.
- Target: `class` in ['tested_positive'] = diabetes by WHO criteria (tested_positive)
- Dropped columns: none
- Leakage notes: No identifier or alternative-target columns; all 8 predictors are measured at the index examination. The outcome uses WHO criteria (2-h post-load glucose >= 200 mg/dl), so 'plas' is criterion-related; index-exam plas never reaches 200 (max 199), consistent with forecasting later onset, so it is kept but expected to dominate. Zeros in plas/pres/skin/insu/mass are missing codes (NaN, imputed in-fold); insu 48.7% missing, skin 29.6%. No exact duplicates; no subject id.

## Indian Liver Patient Dataset (ILPD) (`ilpd`)

- Source: UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 225 (donors B. Ramana, N. Venkateswarlu; donated 2012-05-20; DOI 10.24432/C5D02C) (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/225/ilpd+indian+liver+patient+dataset.zip)
- SHA-256: `60e18fbfe7f84daf58c178ea280ba5fe8db7e2507aabce01b57425b3b822cf0b`
- Licence: CC BY 4.0
- Provenance: Real clinical records: 583 patients from north-east Andhra Pradesh, India (UCI page); routine liver-function tests plus age and sex; Age capped at 90. The UCI page says 584 records and no missing values, but the file has 583 rows and 4 blank A/G Ratio cells.
- Target: `Selector` in ['1'] = liver patient (Selector = 1)
- Dropped columns: none
- Leakage notes: No identifier or outcome columns. The Selector label was likely assigned using these same liver tests (incorporation bias), so discrimination is optimistic versus screening; hospital case-control-like sample (71% positive). 13 exact duplicate rows (adjacent pairs, same label): the benchmark keeps identical rows in the same fold. A/G Ratio ~ ALB/(TP-ALB) is redundant. 3 rows have DB > TB (implausible, kept as-is).

## Heart Failure Clinical Records (`heart_failure`)

- Source: UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 519 (doi:10.24432/C5Z89R); Chicco & Jurman 2020, BMC Med Inform Decis Mak 20:16; original data Ahmad et al. 2017, PLoS ONE 12(7):e0181001 (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/519/heart+failure+clinical+records.zip)
- SHA-256: `f0739603e2f9573ffc7d509573cbf9bcb4cc889e4eea0f35a75bec68fc9163d7`
- Licence: CC BY 4.0 (UCI dataset page)
- Provenance: Real clinical: records of 299 heart-failure patients (LVSD, NYHA III/IV), Faisalabad Institute of Cardiology and Allied Hospital, Pakistan, Apr-Dec 2015 (Chicco & Jurman 2020; file matches sex split, age range and follow-up range). 25 platelets values equal 263358.03 = mean of the other values (upstream mean imputation): read as missing and imputed in-fold.
- Target: `DEATH_EVENT` in ['1'] = died during the follow-up period (DEATH_EVENT = 1)
- Dropped columns: `time`: outcome leakage: follow-up period in days, not known at baseline and ended by the outcome (median 44.5 vs 172 days, r = -0.53 with DEATH_EVENT)
- Leakage notes: `time` dropped. The file is sorted by `time`, so row order correlates with the label: folds are shuffled and the row index is never a feature. Label = death within a variable 4-285-day follow-up (censored survivors labelled 0: label noise). Blood-value timing undocumented; treated as baseline.

## Parkinson's disease voice measurements (Little et al.) (`parkinsons`)

- Source: UCI Machine Learning Repository, id 174 (doi:10.24432/C59C74) (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/174/parkinsons.zip)
- SHA-256: `9baccfbcdac15d6d9347b37c2a352fb31d65c52e367df5a47d7543a55c75b0ab`
- Licence: CC BY 4.0 (UCI page); cite Little et al. 2007 BioMed Eng OnLine 6:23 and Little et al. 2009 IEEE TBME
- Provenance: Real clinical: sustained-phonation recordings (National Centre for Voice and Speech, Denver), dysphonia features by M. Little (Oxford); donated 2008. File: 195 recordings from 32 subject codes (24 PD, 8 healthy); parkinsons.names says 31 people.
- Target: `status` in ['1'] = Parkinson's disease (status = 1)
- Dropped columns: `name`: identifier (subject code + recording number, e.g. phon_R01_S01_1); used only for the group key
- Leakage notes: Repeated measures: 195 recordings from 32 subjects (6-7 each); status constant within subject. Folds are grouped by subject (StratifiedGroupKFold) via group_regex on `name`. Jitter:DDP = 3 x MDVP:RAP and Shimmer:DDA = 3 x Shimmer:APQ3 (collinear pairs, kept as published).
- Group-aware folds: `name` / `^phon_R01_(S\d{2})_\d+$`

## Early Stage Diabetes Risk Prediction (`early_diabetes`)

- Source: UCI Machine Learning Repository #529 (doi:10.24432/C5VG8H); Islam, Ferdousi, Rahman & Bushra (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/529/early+stage+diabetes+risk+prediction+dataset.zip)
- SHA-256: `67594c0f11257688b57493798e70737b7156ba37a2e6ac75507ae3a35221a388`
- Licence: CC BY 4.0
- Provenance: Real patient survey: questionnaires from patients of Sylhet Diabetes Hospital, Bangladesh, approved by a doctor (UCI page). Hospital-based, case-control-like sample. 269/520 rows are exact duplicates of an earlier row (251 unique, no label conflicts); kept as published, grouped in CV.
- Target: `class` in ['Positive'] = diabetes (class == Positive)
- Dropped columns: none
- Leakage notes: No identifier or post-diagnosis column. 269/520 exact duplicate rows: the benchmark keeps identical rows in the same fold. Respondents were diabetes-hospital patients, so symptom recall may reflect known status; Polyuria/Polydipsia are near-diagnostic. Obesity is a Yes/No judgement, not BMI.

## Mammographic Mass (UCI 161) (`mammographic`)

- Source: UCI Machine Learning Repository, id 161 (doi:10.24432/C53K6Z) (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/161/mammographic+mass.zip)
- SHA-256: `4c5158166aa7f1503e14d95be4c95fe66a734474f614441ede226314b93db6e7`
- Licence: CC BY 4.0 (UCI dataset page); cite Elter (2007), doi:10.24432/C53K6Z
- Provenance: Real clinical: 961 masses on full-field digital mammograms, Institute of Radiology, University Erlangen-Nuremberg, 2003-2006; donated 2007 by M. Elter (Elter et al., Med. Phys. 34:4164, 2007).
- Target: `severity` in ['1'] = malignant mass (severity = 1)
- Dropped columns: `bi_rads`: outcome leakage: radiologists' double-read BI-RADS final assessment (UCI: 'non-predictive'), a malignancy judgement summarising the other descriptors; code 6 = biopsy-proven cancer; invalid codes 0 and 55 present
- Leakage notes: BI-RADS dropped. Shape, margin and density are BI-RADS descriptors read before biopsy. Population: masses already referred to biopsy/follow-up, not screening. 353 duplicate (X, y) rows (542 distinct patterns): identical rows kept in the same fold.

## Differentiated Thyroid Cancer Recurrence (UCI 915) (`dtc_recurrence`)

- Source: UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 915 (DOI 10.24432/C5632J) (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/915/differentiated+thyroid+cancer+recurrence.zip)
- SHA-256: `66007e38af856f439fc5e8d1bfd49db4e3cd963723f0b4d363e61f4bdd7bab11`
- Licence: CC BY 4.0 (UCI page); credit Borzooei & Tarokhian, DOI 10.24432/C5632J
- Provenance: Real clinical: retrospective cohort of 383 patients with well-differentiated thyroid cancer followed >= 10 years, Hamadan University of Medical Sciences, Iran (Borzooei et al. 2023, doi:10.1007/s00405-023-08299-w).
- Target: `Recurred` in ['Yes'] = recurrence of differentiated thyroid cancer (Recurred = Yes)
- Dropped columns: `Response`: outcome leakage: ATA response-to-therapy category assessed during follow-up, not at diagnosis; overlaps the target (Structural Incomplete 89/91 recurred, Excellent 1/208)
- Leakage notes: Response dropped. Kept columns are available by the end of initial diagnosis/treatment (post-operative prognosis task, not screening). Risk and Stage are composites of other kept columns. Near-deterministic categories: Risk=High 32/32, M1 18/18 recurred. 26 duplicate encoded rows (one profile carries both labels): identical rows kept in the same fold.

## Chronic Kidney Disease (UCI 336) (`ckd`)

- Source: UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 336 (Rubini, Soundarapandian & Eswaran, 2015; DOI 10.24432/C5G020); UCI's processed CSV export (the zip holds a .rar) (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/336/data.csv)
- SHA-256: `0eeea8d17f5ad8792d854999d6ddf1602ec4e116616f6ccdfdaef0ba8109e694`
- Licence: CC BY 4.0 (UCI dataset page)
- Provenance: Real clinical: 400 patient records (24 clinical/lab attributes) collected from a hospital over ~2 months, donated July 2015. Case-control style (250 ckd / 150 notckd), not a screening cohort.
- Target: `class` in ['ckd'] = ckd (chronic kidney disease)
- Dropped columns: none
- Leakage notes: No column derived from the label. sc and al are KDIGO diagnostic criteria (kept). Case-control design: every notckd row is normal on every attribute, so classes are nearly separable (hemo alone ~0.93 accuracy): expect AUC near 1 and a ceiling effect. Missingness depends on class (impute in-fold, no missing indicators). Implausible values kept as recorded. Stray tabs handled by strip().

## Thyroid disease: sick euthyroid vs negative (Garvan Institute, OpenML 38 'sick') (`thyroid_sick`)

- Source: OpenML data_id 38 'sick' v1 (UCI Thyroid Disease id 102; Garvan Institute, Sydney / J. R. Quinlan) (https://openml.org/data/v1/download/38/sick.arff)
- SHA-256: `85c39615380ca4c05c17a53c3faad9523924958d1e9bc5af0dcbefc6339e7800`
- Licence: CC BY 4.0 (UCI Thyroid Disease, id 102, DOI 10.24432/C5D010); OpenML data_id 38 lists 'Public'; cite Quinlan (1986)
- Provenance: Real clinical thyroid-function referrals, Garvan Institute (Sydney) via J. R. Quinlan, 1987. Raw MD5 ee5cb4b7f41a5f44b0cd234f675ab492 equals OpenML's md5_checksum.
- Target: `Class` in ['sick'] = sick (sick euthyroid syndrome)
- Dropped columns: `TBG`: >50% missing: 100% missing (never measured); `TBG_measured`: constant: 'f' in all 3772 rows; `hypopituitary`: near-constant: 't' in 1 of 3772 rows; `TSH_measured`: duplicates the lab value's missingness; test-ordering flag encodes clinician suspicion and the work-up behind the label; `T3_measured`: duplicates the lab value's missingness; test-ordering flag encodes clinician suspicion and the work-up behind the label; `TT4_measured`: duplicates the lab value's missingness; test-ordering flag encodes clinician suspicion and the work-up behind the label; `T4U_measured`: duplicates the lab value's missingness; test-ordering flag encodes clinician suspicion and the work-up behind the label; `FTI_measured`: duplicates the lab value's missingness; test-ordering flag encodes clinician suspicion and the work-up behind the label
- Leakage notes: The label (sick euthyroid) was assigned from this same thyroid panel plus clinical context: expect high AUC. *_measured flags dropped, but missingness of kept labs still differs by class (T3 missing 21.6% of negatives vs 1.3% of positives); imputed in-fold without indicators. The 'sick' input is a referral-form flag of non-thyroidal illness, not the label. referral_source acts as a site proxy. 61 exact duplicate records (all negative) kept in the same fold. 6.1% positive.

## Cervical Cancer (Risk Factors) (`cervical`)

- Source: UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 383 (K. Fernandes, J. S. Cardoso, J. Fernandes; 2017; DOI 10.24432/C5Z310) (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/383/cervical+cancer+risk+factors.zip)
- SHA-256: `d86f38fbb1f4c40c22c240127875d7a83a2f96238f7ed5a388e2277cfb79a742`
- Licence: CC BY 4.0
- Provenance: Real clinical/survey data: 858 patients at Hospital Universitario de Caracas, Venezuela (Fernandes, Cardoso & Fernandes, IbPRIA 2017); '?' marks questions patients declined to answer.
- Target: `Biopsy` in ['1'] = positive biopsy (Biopsy = 1)
- Dropped columns: `Hinselmann`: alternative target / outcome leakage: colposcopy result from the same work-up as the biopsy; `Schiller`: alternative target / outcome leakage: Schiller test result from the same work-up; `Citology`: alternative target / outcome leakage: cytology result from the same work-up; `STDs: Time since first diagnosis`: >50% missing (91.7%); `STDs: Time since last diagnosis`: >50% missing (91.7%); `STDs:cervical condylomatosis`: constant (0 in all non-missing rows); `STDs:AIDS`: constant (0 in all non-missing rows)
- Leakage notes: Target is Biopsy only. Dx:* kept: prior diagnoses from the medical history, known at the screening visit (Dx:Cancer = 1 in 18 rows, 6 biopsy-positive). Missingness is outcome-associated (Hormonal Contraceptives '?' in 13.4% of negatives vs 0% of positives): imputed in-fold without indicators. Redundant indicator/count pairs kept for in-fold selection. Donor-imputed constants kept as-is. 26 duplicate encoded rows kept in the same fold. 6.4% positive.

## Hepatitis (UCI id 46): survival of hepatitis patients (`hepatitis`)

- Source: UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 46 (donor G. Gong, CMU, via B. Cestnik; 1988; DOI 10.24432/C5Q59J) (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/46/hepatitis.zip)
- SHA-256: `8573c2898714fb32ef8162291dcabd483a1ba9701123cab262f5acace3112d87`
- Licence: CC BY 4.0
- Provenance: Real clinical records: 155 hepatitis patients with vital status (DIE 32 / LIVE 123), history, examination and liver-panel tests (Diaconis & Efron 1983; Cestnik et al. 1987). No identifiers.
- Target: `Class` in ['1'] = DIE (Class = 1)
- Dropped columns: none
- Leakage notes: Yes/no codes are undocumented; the data fit 1 = yes (ASCITES raw 1: 14/20 died vs 17/130). Turney's costs/hepatitis.delay marks history/exam items and HISTOLOGY 'immediate', labs 'delayed'; nothing is documented as recorded after death. HISTOLOGY may be a care-process proxy. STEROID/ANTIVIRALS are treatments (confounding by indication). PROTIME 43.9% missing (< 50%, kept). Minority 32: wide intervals expected.

## Statlog (Heart) (`statlog_heart`)

- Source: UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 145 (ESPRIT StatLog project), DOI 10.24432/C57303 (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/145/statlog+heart.zip)
- SHA-256: `04e44018af4f4b32008029fbfb1079e112d3b372bb032dd1ae361c74d7528b2c`
- Licence: CC BY 4.0 (UCI dataset page)
- Provenance: Real clinical, but NOT independent: all 270 rows equal a Cleveland row on all 13 features with the same binary label (checked against processed.cleveland.data); a subset of the complete Cleveland rows.
- Target: `class` in ['2'] = heart disease present (class 2)
- Dropped columns: none
- Leakage notes: Complete overlap with Cleveland: pipeline/reproducibility sanity check only, never external validation, never in the statistics.
